_comment: klt erc supply spec for the bias_core full-cell assembly -- the T1
item 11 (power delivery, structural) supply-spec read for this repo
(issue #66), graded into the tracker via manifests/ (see
manifests/README.md's item-11 row).
Reproduce from the repo root (the recorded command for the committed
erc.json -- the paths are echoed verbatim into the report's `file` and
`spec` fields and are resolved repo-root-relative by `klt signoff`'s
evidence reader, so run it from there exactly as written):
klt erc layout/bias_core/bias_core.gds \
layout/bias_core/erc-supply-spec.json \
--format json > layout/bias_core/erc.json
The run deliberately omits `--pdk`, matching the fleet's item-11 worked
example (gf180-drone-fc's layout/digital/erc-supply-spec.json): the
antenna-ratio grading is not this item's subject (klayout-tools
docs/cli/erc.md -> 'Item 11 does not grade the ERC envelope's own
status'; an antenna verdict is a real defect but does not block item
11, klayout-tools#1994). With no `--pdk` the exit code is therefore
always 4 ('not_checked' -- the antenna question was never asked,
klayout-tools docs/cli/erc.md's exit codes) while the *structural*
read the item grades is the payload's `erc_status`, which reports
"clean"/"violations" independently of any antenna table
(klayout-tools#2179). Read `erc_status`, not the exit code.
What this spec asserts, and why each piece is shaped this way:
- `stackup[0]` MUST carry `role: "gate"` (klt erc's own contract), so
the stack starts at poly rather than at li1. `active_layer` set to
sky130's diffusion layer (65/20, `diff.drawing`) makes the antenna
denominator `poly AND diff` instead of raw poly area, which keeps
tie/decap/filler poly bars -- real poly with no gate oxide -- out of
`gates[]` entirely (klayout-tools#1979). Layer numbers verified
against BOTH the installed PDK's own libs.tech/klayout/tech/sky130A.lyp
(poly.drawing 66/20, diff.drawing 65/20, li1.drawing 67/20,
met1..met4.drawing 68/20..71/20, licon1.drawing 66/44, mcon 67/44,
via 68/44, via2 69/44, via3 70/44) AND klayout-tools' curated sky130
deck layer table (src/klayout_tools/decks/sky130.py) -- the two agree
on every entry. They are NOT copied from another PDK's spec.
- li1/met1/met2/met3/met4 are the routing levels this GDS actually
uses (klt layers on bias_core.gds: 67/20, 68/20, 69/20, 70/20, 71/20
all present; met5/72/20 absent, so it is not declared). via4/71/44 is
absent from the stream for the same reason.
- `label_layer` is declared on li1 (67/5), met1 (68/5) and met3 (70/5)
only -- the three pin-text layers of this GDS that carry supply text
(67/5: VDD/VSS/vdd/vss; 68/5: VSS/vdd/vss; 70/5: vdd at the passives
met3 landing). met2 (69/5) and met4 (71/5) carry signal-pin text only
(n2/na/nkg/pb/pg/tok and nokx/pg), so declaring them would add
nothing -- the same per-layer-only-if-it-carries-relevant-text
discipline as the gf180-drone-fc worked example.
- `nets[]`: VDD and VSS with `kind: "supply"`, named EXACTLY as the
composed cell's own interface spells them (.subckt bias_core VDD VSS
IBIAS VREF BIAS_OK, and compose.request/response.json's top-level
ports). Matching is case-sensitive and per-label-text (klayout-tools
docs/cli/erc.md: 'matched against stackup label text the same way klt
power's power_nets are matched'), so the declared names match the two
stub-promoted top-level pins (67/5 'VDD' at (-100,10)um and 'VSS' at
(-104,14)um) that ride the composed supply rails. The lowercase
'vdd'/'vss' texts in this stream are sub-block-local pin texts the
composition stamps into the top-level frame at each block's own
LOCAL coordinates, not translated by its placement origin -- a
labeling artifact of the same untranslated-frame family #69 fixed
for the route landings (see layout/bias_core/README.md -
Placement): pre-#69 both the texts and the landings missed the real
pads, so they named nothing; post-#69 the routes and the top-level
promoted pins land on the real pads, and the committed pad-point
island census (layout/bin/pad-island-census.py, evidence at
layout/bias_core/pad-island-census.json) shows each declared supply
as ONE island that also carries the sub-block pads' lowercase
aliases (expanded island names 'VDD,vdd' / 'VSS,vss') -- i.e. the
routes genuinely reach every block's internal supply network. The
case-sensitive declared names still resolve exactly, and the
lowercase aliases deliberately stay undeclared. Each declared
supply must resolve to exactly ONE
electrical island: erc.unconnected_net fires on zero matches AND on
more than one, so ZERO findings of that rule is exactly the
'one island per supply' verdict, not merely an absence. A short
between the two would report as erc.supply_short because both are
declared kind: supply.
- There is deliberately NO `ties[]` section here, and the reasons are
recorded rather than implicit. History first: this spec family used
to omit ties[] because `klt erc`'s tie well-conductor collapse
produced a false erc.supply_short on real routed layouts -- filed
upstream as klayout-tools#2169 and FIXED in the pinned klt build
(2b1e55e51bb8, fixed by klayout-tools#2186: a declared well is never a
conductor, the tie graph is isolated, and `tap_requires` exists), so
that historical reason no longer applies by itself. The operative
reasons on THIS block today:
- sky130's p-type substrate is a native substrate with NO drawn
well layer, so a substrate (VSS) tie declaration is structurally
impossible in klt erc today (klayout-tools#2186's documented
remaining limitation: 'a native substrate with no drawn well
layer still cannot declare a substrate tie at all'). Half of the
well-tie question is therefore undeclarable, not computed.
- a nwell->VDD declaration was probed empirically on this exact
GDS before this spec was first committed, and re-probed after
#69's landing fix against the re-composed stream: pre-#69 it
reported 18 erc.missing_tie findings (one per merged nwell
polygon, 0/18 taps reaching the declared net -- the supply
routes then touched none of the blocks' internal networks, so
no tap could reach the net named VDD); post-#69 the same probe
reports exactly 2 findings, both on the two PNP device-group
blocks' collector/base tubs (bias_core_pnp8_leg,
bias_core_xq1_xqr), whose wells tie to their own nodes' local
geometry by design -- the already-tracked #1894 ec/er strap
question covers them, not item 11. Every other merged nwell now
has taps reaching VDD through the connected supply network
itself, which is the direct #69 outcome. The 2 remaining
findings name design-legitimate state rather than a wiring
gap, so declaring ties[] here would still commit findings
rather than evidence -- but the probe's split is now
mechanical (2, not 18, both on the PNP blocks), recorded here so
a future tie declaration can cite the delta.
Omitting ties[] means erc.missing_tie is NOT COMPUTED by this run
(klayout-tools docs/cli/erc.md: 'Omitted entirely ->
erc.missing_tie is never computed') -- its zero count in the
committed report is an absence of evidence, not evidence of
absence. The stand-in well-tie/supply evidence that does exist is
named in manifests/README.md's item-11 row: PG pin labels in the
committed GDS (the VSS/VSS pin text on 68/5, the VDD/VSS stub
labels on 67/5), 30 tap shapes drawn on 65/44 inside 18 merged
nwell polygons (klt layers), and the three device-group sub-block
LVS matches (layout/bias_core_mirror_amp/lvs.json,
layout/bias_core_settle_flag/lvs.json, layout/bias_core_startup/
lvs.json -- status: match) whose net_correspondence pairs
layout-side VDD/VSS to reference-side VDD/VSS pins, i.e. the
supplies were part of a passing device-level compare at
sub-block scope.
Provenance note: the committed erc.json was generated with klt
0.5.0+g2b1e55e51bb8 (a local build of exactly the rev CI pins in
.github/workflows/signoff-manifest.yml; the local build's
'.dirty' suffix in provenance.klt_version is the only
local-vs-remote difference -- no CI byte-compares this envelope)
against layout/pdk.json's pinned sky130A install. layout/pdk.json's
klt_version_pin (0.4.0) deliberately stays untouched: it is the
provenance pin for the drc/extract/lvs chain that predates the ERC
evidence, and re-bumping it means re-rendering that whole chain
(its README-documented discipline), not this issue's scope.
